caption: The drawing features a single object that resembles a stylized beetle or insect, depicted in shades of brown and gray with black accents. The body is elongated and divided into segments, with a textured and patterned surface along the back and sides, giving it a slightly metallic or carved appearance. Two long, curved antennae extend from the head, each ending in a rounded tip and pointing upwards and outward. The object has six short, thick legs positioned along the bottom of the body. The drawing is centered on a plain, light beige or off-white background. In the bottom right corner, there is a small inset diagram showing the object's proportion and orientation, along with the handwritten text "SERIES A Frame #16." Additional small notations, such as “BOLT-JACK,” appear beneath the main illustration, and “R. Horton, Del. 1851” is written near the lower left edge. The whole drawing is framed with a thin line near the edge of the paper.
title: Bootjack
